items.q: What if the system is wrong?
items.a: It does make mistakes — like any system, and we don't hide it: losing trades are shown in the app right next to winning ones. That's why every trade has a stop — a price where it closes with a small loss — and each trade uses only part of the account. The idea is that winners outweigh losers over time, but there are no guarantees.

items.q: What happens if CRYPTO NOVA shuts down?
items.a: Your money won't be affected: it's in your exchange account, not with us. You would simply stop seeing the signals and lessons in the app. That's exactly why we don't hold other people's money.

items.q: Do you need my passwords or keys?
items.a: No! Never share your passwords, SMS codes or your wallet's seed phrase — CRYPTO NOVA never asks for them. If someone writes in our name and asks for that, it's a scammer. The app doesn't need any keys to your exchange.

items.a: The system doesn't trade all the time — only when it sees its signal. The main strategy, for example, waits for a sharp sell-off on heavy volume, and those moments are rare. No trade is a decision too: better to wait than to enter at random. The current status is on the “Futures” tab.

items.q: What is the Piggy bank and why bitcoin?
items.a: The Piggy bank means buying a little at a time, regularly: for example, $10 a week, with a goal and a time frame. In the app it's a learning model: it shows how much you would have saved at real bitcoin prices. Why bitcoin: it's the largest and oldest cryptocurrency, there will never be more than 21 million coins, and after every past deep drop it later set a new record. But the past doesn't guarantee the future.
alt: How does the Piggy bank work?

items.a: Spot means buying the coins themselves, with no borrowing and no leverage: what you buy is yours. The “Spot” tab has CRYPTO NOVA's long-term spot portfolio: a core of bitcoin, ether and solana, large altcoins and a reserve in dollars; in PUBLIC mode these are the coins of the real account on OKX. The system itself keeps the shares from getting lopsided.

A futures contract is a trade on the price move: you don't buy the coin itself, you profit from a rise (long) or a fall (short). Often with leverage, so both profit and loss grow faster. The “Futures” tab shows the system's trades of this kind, with an entry, a stop and a target; in PUBLIC mode these are the real account's trades on OKX.

items.q: Why can't I see the exchange link?
items.a: If OKX and BingX don't operate in your country, the US for example, the app shows no exchange link: we don't offer what isn't allowed where you are. Learning, demo, the Piggy bank and me, NOVA, work fully, and the system's trades are visible in the app. The availability of copy trading and of some instruments depends on your country and region — OKX shows the terms.

Leverage is money borrowed from the exchange for a trade. With 5× leverage, $100 trades like $500: a 1% price move already means a 5% gain or loss. If the price moves hard against you, the exchange closes the trade itself — that's liquidation, and you can lose what you put in. So use leverage only carefully and always with a stop.

items.q: Why is the real account's leverage only 2x?
items.a: On CRYPTO NOVA's real account the leverage is 2x: the system's rules set it, with a cap of 3x. Leverage doesn't change the amount at risk: the trade size comes from the stop, and one trade risks at most 1% of the futures budget. Higher leverage would only lower the margin and bring liquidation closer, and the trades' stops can be 6–12% away. The signals show 2x–5x: that's the rule's own label — the farther the stop, the lower the leverage.

A stop, or stop-loss, is a price chosen in advance where the trade closes with a small loss so it doesn't grow. Like a seat belt: it won't save you from scratches, but it keeps a crash from hurting too much. Every CRYPTO NOVA trade has a stop. In a sharp jump it sometimes fills a little worse than the set price.

Long is a bet on the price rising: buy lower, sell higher. Short is a bet on it falling: you earn if the price goes down. Futures allow both, so the system can earn in a falling market too. But it can also be wrong in either direction.

A stablecoin is a digital dollar on a blockchain: 1 coin is worth about $1, for example USDT or USDC. It's handy for keeping a reserve and sending money around the world quickly. In July 2025 the US signed the GENIUS Act into law — the first federal rules for stablecoins. But it's not a bank deposit: who issues it matters.

Learning has 4 levels, from complete beginner to advanced: 52 lessons with real-life examples and quizzes, 4–5 minutes each. Start with the first level. How the app itself works is shown by the short tour on the Home screen.

Bitcoin is the first and largest cryptocurrency — digital money with no bank in the middle. It has worked since 2009, and transfers are recorded on the blockchain — a shared ledger that can't be secretly rewritten. There will never be more than 21 million coins, which is why it's often called digital gold.

items.q: Why is everyone talking about the future of crypto?
items.a: Because crypto is going from niche to mainstream! Since January 2024 you can buy bitcoin in the US through exchange-traded funds, and the biggest investors have come in. In March 2026 the SEC approved a Nasdaq pilot for tokenized stocks, and from late October 2026 Samsung lets Galaxy users in the US keep USDC digital dollars right in their wallet. These are big steps, but the price can still fall hard.
alt: Why has bitcoin kept rising for years?

items.a: An ETF is a fund that trades on a stock exchange like an ordinary share. A spot bitcoin ETF holds real bitcoins, and an investor buys it through a regular broker. In the US such funds were approved on 10 January 2024, and in October 2026 they held about 1 293 000 BTC. That's how big funds and cautious investors came into crypto.
alt: Why do big funds buy bitcoin?

items.a: It's when a share gets a digital twin on a blockchain: it moves faster and can trade longer than normal exchange hours. In June 2025 Robinhood launched tokens of 200+ US stocks and ETFs for the EU, and in March 2026 the SEC approved a Nasdaq pilot with tokenized stocks. The stock market and crypto are gradually meeting on the same technology.

items.q: Is it too late to buy bitcoin?
items.a: People asked this at $13 in 2013, at $1 000 and at $20 000. Nobody knows the future price, but the world is clearly moving toward crypto: exchange-traded funds, tokenized stocks, digital dollars in wallets. To avoid guessing the moment, many people buy a little at a time, regularly — like in the Piggy bank. This is not financial advice.

items.q: Bitcoin dropped — is this the end?
items.a: Bitcoin's history is full of deep drops: after the peaks of 2011, 2013, 2017 and 2021 it lost 75–93% — and each time it later set a new record. The latest record is $126 210, on 6 October 2025. Drops are part of the journey, but the past doesn't guarantee the future, so only invest what you're ready to hold for a long time.

items.q: What does a trade's result mean?
items.a: It's how much the trade made or lost in dollars. For a closed trade it's the final result after the exit; for an open one it's the current profit or loss, which moves with the price. The percent next to it shows how much the coin's price changed, and that isn't the same as a percent of the account: with leverage a trade moves faster than the price. So judge the system by the whole portfolio.

Spot means buying the coins themselves, with no debt: what you buy is yours, and you can hold it as long as you like. A futures trade is a bet on the price move: you can earn on a rise (long) or on a fall (short), often with leverage, so profits and losses both grow faster. In CRYPTO NOVA spot is the base of the portfolio, futures are the smaller part, and every futures trade has a stop.
